name: Moravia
summary: Moravia sits mostly in the warm Pannonian zone, with continental influence. Vines grow on loess, limestone and sands; about two thirds of the area is white, giving aromatic whites with fresh acidity and soft, fruity reds.
label_note: Quality wine needs at least 15 °NM must weight. Predicate wines (jakostní víno s přívlastkem) rise by ripeness: kabinetní víno 19 °NM, pozdní sběr 21, výběr z hroznů 24, výběr z bobulí, ledové víno and slámové víno 27, výběr z cibéb 32.

grapes.name: Grüner Veltliner
grapes.local_note: Veltlínské zelené; about 1,365 ha in Morava at 31 Dec 2025, the most planted

grapes.name: Graševina
grapes.local_note: Ryzlink vlašský; strongest in the Mikulovská subregion

grapes.name: Blaufränkisch
grapes.local_note: Frankovka; the most planted red, strongest in Velkopavlovická

appellations.name: Mikulovská
appellations.note: PDO subregion; about 4,827 ha at 31 Dec 2025, the largest, mostly white.

appellations.name: Velkopavlovická
appellations.note: PDO subregion; about 4,468 ha, with the most red vineyard of any subregion.

appellations.name: Slovácká
appellations.note: PDO subregion; about 3,992 ha in the east.

appellations.name: Znojemská
appellations.note: PDO subregion; about 2,953 ha in the southwest, mostly white.

appellations.name: VOC Znojmo
appellations.note: VOC since 2009 for Sauvignon, Ryzlink rýnský and Veltlínské zelené; Znojmo lies in the Znojemská subregion.

appellations.name: VOC Valtice
appellations.note: VOC since 2015 for Ryzlink rýnský, Sylvánské zelené and Rulandské modré; Valtice lies in the Mikulovská subregion.

appellations.name: VOC Bzenec
appellations.note: VOC since 2017 for Ryzlink rýnský and Rulandské bílé; Bzenec lies in the Slovácká subregion.

appellations.name: VOC Mutěnice
appellations.note: VOC since 2018 for Ryzlink rýnský, Sylvánské zelené, Tramín červený and Zweigeltrebe; Mutěnice lies in the Slovácká subregion.

appellations.name: VOC Kyjov
appellations.note: VOC since 2023 for Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir; Kyjov lies in the Slovácká subregion.

name: Dealu Mare
summary: Hill vineyards in Prahova and Buzău counties, one of Romania's best known wine districts. Iron rich red clays suit its reds, which are known above all for Fetească Neagră.
label_note: The name may be followed by one of eight official sub-designations, such as Dealu Mare-Urlați, and then by a single vineyard name.

grapes.name: Fetească Neagră
grapes.local_note: The grape the district is best known for.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare-Boldești
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin in Prahova County.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare-Valea Călugărească
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin in Prahova County.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare-Urlați
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin in Prahova County.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare-Ceptura
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin in Prahova County.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare-Tohani
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin in Prahova County.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare-Breaza
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin in Buzău County.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare-Merei
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin in Buzău County.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare-Zorești
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin in Buzău County.

name: Cotnari
summary: Vineyards in Iași County, in Romania's historic Moldavia region, famous for golden sweet white wines touched by noble rot. Dry whites come from native grapes such as Fetească Albă and Frâncușă.
label_note: The label may add one of 24 official single vineyard names, such as Dealul Castel or Dealul Paraclis.

grapes.name: Grasă de Cotnari
grapes.local_note: The grape behind the famous sweet wines.

name: Murfatlar
summary: Vineyards on limestone soils in Dobrogea, between the Danube and the Black Sea, among Romania's sunniest and driest. Wines run from dry to sweet, including ripe reds and late harvest whites.
label_note: The sub-designation Medgidia or Cernavodă may accompany the name, and a single vineyard name such as Basarabi may be added.

appellations.name: Medgidia
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin, used with or without the Murfatlar name.

appellations.name: Cernavodă
appellations.note: Sub-designation of origin, used with or without the Murfatlar name.

name: Melnik
summary: Warm valley vineyards in south western Bulgaria near the Greek border, open to Mediterranean influence and mostly on sandy soils over limestone. The reds, led by the local Melnik grapes, are spicy and peppery with firm tannins.
label_note: Registered as Мелник; the PDO may also be labelled with the traditional term GKNP (guaranteed and controlled appellation of origin).

grapes.name: Shiroka Melnishka
grapes.local_note: Grown almost only in the Struma valley.

grapes.name: Ranna Melnishka Loza
grapes.local_note: Also sold as Melnik 55, a crossing of Shiroka Melnishka and Valdiguié.

appellations.name: Melnik
appellations.note: PDO covering villages in the Sandanski, Petrich, Strumyani and Kresna municipalities; red, rosé and, since 2023, white.

appellations.name: Sandanski
appellations.note: PDO for red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon only.

appellations.name: Trakiyska nizina
appellations.note: PGI (Thracian Lowlands) whose area includes the Petrich, Sandanski, Kresna and Strumyani municipalities.

name: Sakar
summary: Vineyards at the foot of the Sakar mountain in Bulgaria's Thracian Lowland. Red wines lead, chiefly from Merlot and Syrah.
label_note: Registered as Сакар; the PDO may also be labelled with the traditional term GKNP (guaranteed and controlled appellation of origin).

appellations.name: Sakar
appellations.note: PDO for red, rosé and white wine from villages around Svilengrad on the south western slopes of the Sakar mountain.

appellations.name: Trakiyska nizina
appellations.note: PGI (Thracian Lowlands) covering the wider plain.

name: Fruška Gora
summary: Vineyards cover the slopes of Fruška Gora, a low range above the Danube, whose nearness helps the grapes ripen. Soils are largely chernozem over loess, and Grašac, the local Welschriesling, has long been grown here.
label_note: Serbian quality wines with geographical origin are labelled K.P.K. (controlled origin and quality) or K.G.P.K. (controlled and guaranteed origin and quality, the top tier).

grapes.name: Graševina
grapes.local_note: Grašac or Italijanski rizling locally; recommended for Fruška gora in the official zoning rulebook

appellations.name: Fruška gora
appellations.note: Vinogorje (Fruškogorsko vinogorje), the only vinogorje of the Srem rejon, on the higher slopes around the national park.

name: Codru
summary: Hilly, forested country in central Moldova, where the woods temper a warm continental climate. Its light soils favour white wines, which make up most of the output, with Merlot also widely grown.
label_note: The main label must carry the wine category and the words cu indicație geografică protejată "Codru".

appellations.name: Codru
appellations.note: PGI for white, rosé, red, liqueur and sparkling wines.

name: Ștefan Vodă
summary: Moldova's south eastern wine region, planted mainly on black earth soils rich in humus. It is above all a red wine region, built on Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and the local Rară Neagră.
label_note: Labels must state vin cu indicație geografică protejată "Ștefan Vodă"; a variety may be named when it makes up at least 85% of the wine.

grapes.name: Băbească Neagră
grapes.local_note: Known in Moldova as Rară Neagră.

appellations.name: Ștefan Vodă
appellations.note: PGI for white, rosé and red wines.

name: Valul lui Traian
summary: Moldova's south western wine region is mainly known for red wines. Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon are the leading grapes, with Fetească Neagră among the local varieties grown there.

appellations.name: Valul lui Traian
appellations.note: PGI.
